aria: Animated recap of the Celtics' 131 to 94 home win over the Mavericks: Jayson Tatum's step-back 3-pointer with 4 seconds left in the third quarter that made it 104 to 71, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Tatum's 32 points, the top scorers, how the Celtics won, and the next game against Orlando.
notes: Box score from the Celtics' 131–94 home win over the Dallas Mavericks at TD Garden on Nov 15, 2026, from the Land of Basketball box score, with the SI.com and CBS Sports play-by-play and game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sports), the Boston Globe, Boston.com, SB Nation (via Yahoo Sports) and Dallas Sports Journal. All 131 Boston points and all 94 Dallas points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 42–9 after one, 67–37 Boston at the half, 104–71 after three. Team totals (field goals 48 of 95 to 33 of 83, threes 23 of 55 to 14 of 41, free throws 12 of 16 to 14 of 17, assists 34–27) are from the box score; rebounds 52–38 are the players' rebounds in the box score. Second-chance points (29–16) and fast-break points (10–17) are from Dallas Sports Journal. Boston's 41-point lead came at 120–79 on a Ron Harper Jr. 3-pointer with 8:20 left (SI.com play-by-play; Dallas Sports Journal). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

The 33-point lead after one quarter was the largest first-quarter lead in Celtics history (AP; Boston Globe). Dallas went 2 of 18 from the field and 0 of 8 from three in the first quarter (Boston Globe). Jayson Tatum scored 21 of his 32 in the third quarter on 6 of 9 shooting with four 3-pointers, including 13 straight Boston points to end it (AP; SI.com play-by-play), and sat out the fourth (Dallas Sports Journal; Boston Globe). It was Boston's sixth straight win (AP; Boston Globe). Kyrie Irving did not play for Dallas (knee management, AP) on the second night of a back-to-back (Dallas Sports Journal). Boston hosts Orlando on Monday, Nov 16 at 7:00 PM ET (Land of Basketball schedule; Boston.com).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jayson Tatum's step-back 3-pointer at the end of the third quarter that made it 104–71 (SB Nation gives 4.3 seconds left, Dallas Sports Journal 4.7; the SI.com play-by-play logs an unassisted step-back three at 0:04 with the score going from 101–71 to 104–71). Boston.com says it came over a triple team. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Boston Celtics or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Tatum's listed 6-foot-8 and 210 pounds (RealGM; Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to a reported 6-foot-11 wingspan (DraftExpress; The Sporting News), in Boston's home white with No. 0 (RealGM). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
